(1877).—B. 1847; Marlborough school; ensign, 32nd regt., 1866; capt., May, 1880; major, 26th Cameroonians, 1881; A.D.C. to the gov. of Mauritius, 1872-74, to gov. of Fiji, 1875; commanded force sent to reduce mountain tribes, 1876 (promoted to company and C.M.G.); comdt. armed native constab., and comsnr. in mountains, 1877; A.D.C. to gov. N. Zealand, 1880, and to gov. of Ceylon, 1883; inspr. gen. of constab., and dir. of prisons, Jamaica, 1886; inspr.-gen. of pol., 'Ceylon, Oct., 1891; inspr.-gen. of pol. and prisons, Sept., 1898; retired, 1902.

KNOWLES, JOSEPH.—Tide waiter, recvr.-gen.'s dept., Bahamas, 1890; res. just. and school-teacher, Ragged Island, 1897; clk., pol. off., Nassau, Sept., 1903.

KNUTSFORD, 1ST VISCOUNT (creat. 1895, created BARON 1888), THE RIGHT HON. SIR HENRY THURSTAN HOLLAND, BART., G.C.M.G. (1896), K.C.M.G. (1877), C.M.G. (1875).—B. 1825; succeeded to the baronetcy on the death of his father in Oct., 1873; ed. at Harrow and Trin. Coll., Camb.; called to the bar, Inner Tem., Nov., 1849, and went to the N. Circuit; legal adviser to the sec. of state for the cols., Jan., 1867, and astl. under-sec. of state, Mar., 1870; resign., 3rd Aug., 1874, and elected mem. for Midhurst, 22nd Sept., 1874; mem. of the roy. coman. on the treatment of fugitive slaves, 1876; one of the roy. comans. on the defence of Br. possessions and commerce abroad, Sept., 1879; sec. to the treasur., June, 1885; and vice-pres. of the coun., Sept., 1885, and again in Aug., 1886; returned to Parlmt. as mem. for the Hampstead div. of Middlesex, 1885, and again 1886 and 1887; sec. of state for the cols., Jan., 1887, to Aug., 1892; pres. pol. confere., 1887.

KOCH, REV. C. A.—Astl. missionary to Bishop of Labuan, bishop's chaplain, regisr. of the diocese, 1866; diocesan chaplain, Ratnapura, Ceylon, Mar., 1866; col. chaplain, Jaffna, Aug., 1869; col. chaplain, Colombo, 1880.

KOCH, HENRY C.—Admitted to Natal bar as solnr., 1884, as advoc., 1887; crown prosecutor and legal adviser to Zululand Govt., Apr., 1889; is also regisr. of deeds, regisr.-gen. of births, deaths, and marriages; master, sup. ct., Natal, 1900; spec. comsnr. for Natal to administer oaths to surrendered burghers; resumed duty as mast., sup. ct., 1902.

KOCH, WILFRED VINCENT MILLE, M.B., C.M. (Edin., 1884), M.D. (Edin., 1895, highest honours, gold medal, thesis).—Late astl. in eye dept. of Edin. roy. infirmary; and astl. to the lectures on diseases of the eye and mental diseases, Edin. Univ.; and astl. to the gynecological dept., Edin. schl. of medicine; clin. astl., Royal London Ophthalmic hosp., 1901; clin. astl., hosp. for diseases of ear, nose, and throat, Golden Sq., 1901; ag. astl. med. offr., W. Riding Asyl., Sheffield, 1884; astl. med. offr., Hull Borough Asyl., 1884-88; late surg. to Monckton and Carlton Main Collieries, Barnaley; astl. surg., col. hosp., Port of Spain, 1889; ag. med. supt., Lepre Asyl., Trinidad, 1890-92; dist. med. offr., Diego Martin, 1890-92; ag. dist. med. offr., Port of Spain, 1892-93; ag. med. supt., Lepre Asyl., 1893; ag. dist. med. offr., Diego Martin, 1893; ag. med. supt., lun. asyl., June to Oct., 1894; in charge of col. hosp., San Fernando, June to Dec., 1899; and of col. hosp.,
Port of Spain, for various periods; ag. dist. med. offr., Couva, 1900; St. Joseph, 1902; lieut., 1891; capt., 1892; comdg. Port of Spain art. volrs.; surg. to permanent staff, Trinidad local forces; major, local force reserve, 1903; asst. surgeon, Hong Kong, 1903; J.P.; ag. med. offr. in charge of gaol and infectious diseases hosp., 1903-4.

KENIG, ETTRIKE.—Crown prosecutor, Mauritius, Nov., 1900; 2nd asst. col. sec., July, 1903; asst. col. sec., 9th Nov., 1903; ag. substitute procureur and advocate-general, 2nd Feb., 1904.

KENIG, LEON.—Senior clk., judicial dept., Seychelles, 2nd June, 1892; ag. 5th cls. clk., col. sec.'s office, Mauritius, in 1897, 1898 and 1899; 5th cls. clk. ditto, 1st July, 1899; 4th cls. ditto, 7th July, 1902; clk. to ex. coun. and coun. of govt., 9th Nov., 1903.

KOLLER, T. W.—Clk., acctns. dept., G.P.O., O.R.C., 1st July, 1900, to 31st Oct., 1902; clk. pub. health dept., 1st to 30th Nov., 1902; examr. of acctns., audit dept., 1st Dec., 1902; is also sec. to tender bd.

KORTRIGHT, L. M.—A.M.I.C.E., M.I.M.E.; surv. of roads and supt. of pub. wks., St. Kitts, 1879; official mem. legis. coun., St. Kitts and Nevis, 1886; J.P., and visiting justice of the gaol; mem. ex. coun., St. Kitts-Nevis, 1901.

KROHN, A. W.—Served in 33rd Co. Army Service Corps, as spec. clk., 1st March to 31st Aug., 1902; stationery dept., O.R.C., 1902.

KYNSLEY, SIR W. R., F.K.Q.C.P., KNT. BACH., C.M.G. 1888.—B. 1840; prin. civ. med. offr., and inspr.-gen. of hospitals, Ceylon, Feb., 1875; ret. 1897.

LABORDE, E. D., I.S.O. (1903).—1st clk., audit office, Tobago, Jan., 1882; dep. regiar., ag. confidential clk., to administrator, and clk. of couns., June, 1882; 2nd clk., administrator's office, St. Lucia, Feb., 1883; ch. clk., Sept., 1883; ag. 2nd clk., gov.-in-chief's office, Barbados, 1884; ch. clk. to gov., Windward Is., 1885; priv. sec. to Gov. Sendall, 1888; ch. of pol. and excise, St. Vincent, 1889; inspr. of prisons, 1889; supervisor of cust. and port offr., 1897; commended in despatches for relief wk. during hurricane, 1898; chmn. town bd., 1899; mem. ex. and legis. couns.; ag. col. sec., Apr. to May, 1901.

LACOSTE, THE HON. SIR ALEXR., K.C., KT. BACH. (1892).—B. 1842; ch. just., Court of King's Bench, Quebec; mem. of the Dominion privy coun., 1892.

LAFFAN, JAMES THOMAS, L.R.C.S.I., L.K., and Q.C.P.I. etc.—Asst.-col. surg., Larnaca, Cyprus, 1883; res. med. offr., Wyndham, W. Australia, 1886; ag. R.M., Wyndham, 1888; res. med. offr., Bunbury, 1889; pol. mag., Blackwood, 1889.

LAGDEN, SIR GODFREY YEATMAN, K.C.M.G. (1897), C.M.G. (1894).—B. 1851; clerk, G.P.O., London, 1869-77, after compet. exam.; clk. to sec. to govt., Transvaal, 1878; priv. sec. to adminstr., 1878-81; sec. to exec. coun., 1880-81; priv. sec. to Sir W. Bellairs and Sir E. Wood, while administering govt., 1881; sec. to Transvaal sub-comsn. for compensation claims, 1881-82; engaged as war correspondent, Egyptian campaign, 1882-3; present at all engagements, including Tel-el-Kebir and capture of Cairo; on special financial duty, G. Coast, 1883; sec. and secttn., Basutoland, 1884; asst. comsnr., 1886; established magistracy in Masupha's country, 1886; acted as res. comsnr., May to Nov., 1890; ag. Br. comsnr., Swaziland govt. comtee. of adminstr., Apr., 1892; res. comsnr., Basutoland, 1893-1901; comsnr. for native affairs, Transvaal, Aug., 1901; mem. of ex. and leg. couns.; chrmn. of S. African inter-col. native affairs comsn., 1903-4.

LAIDLAW, ROBERT, M.D. (Aberdeen).—Asst. med. offr., Seychelles, 21st Jan., 1902; J.P., and chairman, local bd. of health, Praslin and La Digue Is., Seychelles.

LAING, ERNEST, ALEX. RONALD.—L.R.C.P., L.R.C.S., Edin., L.F.P.S., Glasgow, 1895; L.M. Rot. Hosp., Dub., 1894; (Queen's Coll., Belfast, Surg. Hall, Edin., and R.C.S., Dub.). Health offr., special plague duty, govt. of Egypt; res. pupil, Jervis-st. Hosp., Dub.; res., Rot. Hosp., Dub.; med. offr., Tardis dist., Bombay, and asst. health offr. on spec. plague duty, Calcutta; asst. surgeon, Hong Kong, 1902; and med. offr. in charge of govt. asylums.

LAING, J. E.—A.M.I.C.E., formerly ch. asst. engrnr. in municipalities of Manchester and Leicestershire; dist. survr., Sheffield; col. survr., S. Leone, Sept., 1894; title changed to dir. of P.W., Nov., 1896.

LAIRD, THE HON. DAVID.—Mem. educn. coun., P.E.I., 1872-3; one of the delega. who negotiated the admission of the island into the Dominion; sworn of the Canadian priv. coun. and min. of interior, 1873-6; lieut.-gov., N.W. Territories, 1876-8; was ch. comsnr. in negotiating treaty with Blackfeet Indians, 1877.

LAMB, BENJAMIN.—Lieut., R.F.A.; served in S. African war, Jan., 1900, to Aug., 1902; A.D.C. and priv. sec. to gov., Barbados, Oct., 1902, to Aug., 1903.

LAMB, JOHN CAMERON, C.B. (1895), C.M.G. (1890).—B. 1845; entered the P.O. in 1864; prin. clk., 1877; was one of the Br. delega. to the submarine cables protection confce. at Paris, May and Dec., 1886; asst. sec. to the P.O., 1889; 1st Br. deleg. to the internat. telegraph confce. at Paris, 1890, when he was also one of the representatives of the Cape and Natal; roy. comsnr. on electrical communication with lighthouses and lightships, June, 1892; 3rd sec. to the P.O., Apr., 1896; sen. Br. deleg. and "president de la commission des tarifs" at internat. telegraph confce. at Budapest, 1896, when he was also one of the representatives of the Cape, Natal, and N. Zealand; 3rd sec. to P.O., Apr., 1896; 2nd sec., Jan., 1897; pres., internat. telegraph confce., London, 1903, and sen. deleg. of U.K., Cape and Natal; also sen. Br. deleg. at internat. confce. on wireless telegraphy, Berlin, 1903.

LAMBERT, HENRY CHARLES MILLER.—Ed. at Eton Coll., and New Coll., Oxford; 1st class in classical mods., 1889; 1st class in final classical schls., 1891; entered as student of Lincoln's Inn; apptd. 2nd class clk. in the C.O. after open compet. exam., Feb., 1892; mem. of comtee. emigrts. information office, 1894; chrmn. of the comtee., 1897; acted as priv. sec. to Mr. Chamberlain for the purposes of the comtee. of the H. of C. on South Africa, 1897; 1st class clk., Nov., 1898.

LAMBTON, STEPHEN HARBORD.—Entered postal service, N.S.W., Sept., 1852; sec., Sept., 1866; dep. postm.-gen.

LAMINGTON, LORD (2nd Baron, creat. 1890), SIR CHARLES WALLACE ALEXANDER NAPIER COCHRANE-BAILLIE, G.C.I.E. (1903), G.C.M.G. (1900), K.C.M.G. (1895).—Only son of 1st baron; born, 1860; dep. lieut. Lanarkshire; lieut. Lanarkshire yeomanry, 1883; M.P. for N. St. Pancras, 1886-90; gov. Queensland, 1895-1901; gov. of Bombay, 1903.

LAMONT, WILLIAM J.—Grad. Moray House Coll., Edin.; entd. imp. custs. by comp. exam.; 1st place in U.K., 1894; superv. of custs., G. Coast,
1896; travelling and inspecting superv., G. Coast, 1901; asst. collr. cust., S. Leone, 1901; ag. collr. cust., 10th May to 17th Oct., 1902; J.P. for Colony.

LAMPSON, P. E.—Ed. Wesleyan mission schl., Anamaboe, G. Coast; asst. master, govt. schl., Accra, 1893.

LANGEVIN, EDUARD JOSEPH, N.P.—Admitted as a notary public, Lower Canada, 3rd Dec., 1858; a mem. of bd. of notaries of Lower Canada for several years; clk. of the Crown in Chancery, Canada, Jan., 1865; to same office for Dominion, July, 1867; dep. regisr.-gen., July, 1868; under-sec. of state of Canada, July, 1873; elected sec. to civ. ser. bd. of Canada, 1876; clk. of the Senate, 1883.

LANGEVIN, THE HON. SIR HECTOR LOUIS, K.C.M.G. (1881), C.B. (1868), K.C., LL.D.—B. 1826; called to the bar of Lower Canada, 1850; created a Q.C., 1864; mayor of Quebec from 1858 to 1861, and as such received H.R.H. the Prince of Wales on his landing in Canada, 1860; entered Canadian parlmt., 1857, and held a seat, first in the old legis. assem. and, since confederation, in the house of commons of the Dominion till 1892; mem. of the exec. coun., Canada, and solr.-gen. for Lower Canada, Mar., 1864; postmr.-gen., Nov., 1866; at confederation, July, 1867, sworn of the Queen's priv. coun. and was apptd. sec. of state of Canada until Dec., 1879, when apptd. min. of pub. wks., and whilst holding that office, was elected as the successor of the late Sir G. E. Cartier, Bart., as leader of the liberal-conservative party of Lower Canada; resig. office, Nov., 1873; postmr.-gen. in Sir John A. Macdonald's 2nd administration, Oct., 1878; then min. of pub. wks.; resig., 1891; was one of the framers of the present Canadian constitution, and in furtherance of the cause of confederation attended the col. confece. at Charlottetown and Quebec in 1864, and in London in 1866, when the Act of Union was carried through the imp. parlmt.; created a Knight Commander of the Roman Order of St. Gregory the Great, 1870; is the author of a prize essay on Canada, and of several other works.

LANGFORD, CHARLES WM.—Issuer, commissariat dept., Barbados, 1868; asst. storekeeper, control dept., Trinidad, Oct., 1869; clk., G.P.O., Trinidad, June, 1871; 2nd ditto, Nov., 1871; 6th clk. rec.-gen.'s office, Jan., 1875; 5th ditto, Feb., 1877; 4th ditto, May, 1878; 3rd ditto, May, 1879; excise officer, Apr., 1884.

LANGFORD, JOHN.—Clk., col. sec.'s office, Fiji, Oct., 1874; ch. clk. and clk. of legis. coun., Jan., 1878; regiar., sup.ct., and curator of intestate estates, June, 1884.

LANGHAM-CARTER, W.—Ed. at Bradfield Coll., Berks.; cadet, S. Sttlmts., 1890; passed final exam. in Malay, Dec., 1892; ag. dist. offr., Malacca, Jan., 1896; dist. offr., prov. Wellesley, Apr., 1897; continued to act at Malacca; ag. collr. of ld. rev. and regist. of deeds, Singapore, Dec., 1898; inspr. prisons, S.S., Jan. to May, 1901; asst. P.M.G., Penang, Dec., 1901; 2nd magis., Sing., Aug., 1902; ag. collr. of land rev., and regist. of deeds, Sing., Sep., 1902; apptd. to cls. III, B, Jan., 1903.

LANSDOWNE, 5TH MARQUIS OF (Gt. Brit., creat., 1784), K.G., G.C.M.G. (1884), G.C.S.I., G.C.I.E.—HENRY CHARLES KEITH FITZ MAURICE, eldest son of the 4th Marquis.—B. 1845; succeeded his father in 1866; was under-sec. for war from Apr., 1872, to Feb., 1874, and under-sec. India Office, May to Aug., 1880; gov.-gen. of Canada, 1883; viceroy of India, Nov., 1888-94; sec. of state for war, July, 1895; sec. of state for foreign affairs, Nov., 1900.

LAPRIMAUDAYE, C., M.V.O. (1903).—Commander, R.N.; capt. of port, Malta, Oct., 1888; supt. of pol., 1890; collr. of cust. with seat in exec. coun. and coun. of govt., 1903.

LARYMORE, CAPT. H. D., C.M.G. (1896).—B. 1867; ed. Westminster; entered Artil. Militia, 1886; lieut., R.A., Dec., 1886; capt., R.A., Sep., 1897; apptd. G. Coast constab., Feb., 1891; adjt., July, 1891; served in Jebu expdn., as staff offr. and sec. to Sir F. Scott; mentioned in despatches, and received thanks of gov. and exec. and legis. couns. of Lagos (medal and clasp); served in Kumasi expdn., 1896, as A.D.C. and headquarters camp commdt., (ment. in desps. and recd. spec. thanks for services; bronze star), ag. res., Kumasi, 1896-97; R.A. India, 1897-1901; R.A., S. Leone, 1901-02; 3rd cl. rea., N. Nigeria, Apr., 1902; 2nd cl. ditto, Oct., 1902; Haiku scholar, Christ's Coll., Camb., 1903.

LASCELLES, ALFRED GEORGE, B.A.—Univ. Coll., Oxon; 2nd class mod. hist.; called to the bar, Inner Temple, 1885; acted on several occasions as pres. of dist. ct. in Cyprus and as puisne judge; pres. of dist. ct., Papho, 1892; ditto, Larnaca, 1893; ag. puisne judge, June, 1895; ag. Queen's advoc., Feb., 1896; pres. dist. ct., Nicosia, 1896; Queen's advoc., 1898; atty.-gen. of Ceylon, 1902.

LASH, JAR. MILLER.—Ed. upper and middle schls., Peckham; schlmr., Kirkdale prison, Liverpool, 1876; gaoler, Grenada, 1880; supt. of prisons, 1890; gov., Glendairy prison, Barbados, 1894.

LAUDER, CHARLES R.—Clk., pres.'s office, Dominica, Dec., 1872; 4th revenue and quarantine offr., Nov., 1874; 3rd ditto, Feb., 1880; 2nd ditto, rum dept. keeper, 1883.

LAUDER, JOHN J.—Ag. 2nd clk., regr. and prov. marshal's off., Dominica, Feb., 1900: 2nd clk., Jan., 1901.

LAURENCE, P. M.—Puisne judge, Griqualand W., Cape Col., 1882; judge pres., 1888.

LAURIER, THE RIGHT HON. SIR WILFRID, P.C., G.C.M.G. (1897).—B. at St. Lin., Quebec, Nov. 20th, 1841; became a B.C.L. of McGill in 1864, and a Q.C. in 1880; entered parlmt., 1871, being elected for Drummond and Athabasca, and was re-elected in 1874 for the same constituency; min. of inland rev. in the Mackenzie ministry, Sept., 1877, which office he held until the resignation of that govt. in 1878. He was defeated at the gen. election of 1878, but was immediately afterwards elected for Quebec E. He was re-elected at the gen. elections in 1878, 1882, 1887, and 1891. Became leader of the Opposition in Canada in 1890, and premier in June, 1896, on the resignation of the govt. of Sir C. Tupper; was present as the representative of Canada in London at H.M.'s Diamond Jubilee; mem. joint internat. high couns., Quebec and Washington, 1898-9.

LAW, A. F. G.—Asst. comen., Cyprus, 1880; pres. dist. ct., Famagusta, 1883; principal forest offr., 1886; mem. legis. coun., 1887; ag. Queen's advoc., 1889; ag. ch. sec., 1890; Queen's advoc., 1892; puisne judge, S. Sttlmts., 1893; ag. ch just., S. S., Apr., 1901; senior puisne judge, Penang, Dec., 1901.

LAWLEY, HON. SIR ARTHUR, K.C.M.G. (1901).—B. 1860; sec. to administrator, S. Rhodesia, May, 1896; deputy-administr., Matabeleland, Nov., 1896; administrator, Matabeleland, Dec., 1898; ag. administrator, Mashonaland, July, 1899; gov. of W. Aust., Jan., 1901; lt.-gov., Transvaal, 15th Aug., 1902; ag. gov. of Transvaal and O.R.C.
and high comsnr., 1903, chrmn. of ex. coun., pres. of leg. coun., mem. I.C.C.

LAWRENCE, W. T.—Asst. priv. sec. to Baron Henry de Worms, parly. sec. to the Bd. of Trade, 1885-6; in same capacity at the C.O., Feb., 1888, to Aug., 1892; attached to the internat. confce. on sugar bounties, 1887-88.

LAWRENCE, JOHN DUNCAN.—Ed. at Clepington schl., Dundee, and civ. serv. coll., Aberdeen; prelim. in arts, (higher mathematics and German) Aberdeen Univ.; govt. trav. schl. master, Falkland Is., Sep., 1896, to Jan., 1902; 2nd asst. opt. of schls., B. Guiana, Oct., 1903.

LAWRENCE, W. C.—Apptd. after exam., 3rd cls. messenger, C.O., 15th Apr., 1904.

LAWRIE, JAS. WM.—Asst. govt. engrnr. survr., Singapore, 12th June, 1883; resigned, 10th Oct., 1884; re-appointed asst. govt. marine survr., 26th Sep., 1887; govt. marine survr., Penang, 9th Mar., 1901.

LAZZARINI, MAJ.-GEN. C. C. JAMES, C.M.G. (1882).—B. 1819; of the Royal Malta Fencible Artillery, decorated for services in connection with the expdn. to Egypt, 1882.

LAYARD, SIR CHARLES PETER, KT. BACH. (1903).—B. 1849; Ed. Cheltenham Coll., and St. John's Coll., Camb.; called to the bar, Inner Temple, June, 1873; advoc. sup. ct., Ceylon, Aug., 1873; solr. gen., July, 1878; ag. atty.-gen., May, 1891, to July, 1892; puisne judge, sup. ct., Oct., 1892; atty.-gen., Nov., 1892; ch. just., 26th Apr., 1902.

LEACH, JOHN VINCENT.—Ed. Stonyhurst Coll., England; admitted solr. sup. ct., Jamaica, 1881; res. mag., 1888.

LEARMONT, CAPT. JOHN HENRY, late capt. 12th Lancers.—Ed. at Eton; staff adjt., S. Australian mounted forces, 1886-89; A.D.C. to Earl of Kintore, 1889; officer's extra musketry certif., Hythe, 1889; priv. sec. and A.D.C. to Sir C. A. Moloney, gov., Lagos, and clk. to exec. and legis. couns., Feb., 1890; inspr. Bahamas constab. (which force he raised in Barbados), Aug., 1891; inspr.-gen. Leeward Is. pol., 1895, and inspecting offr. of defence forces; J.P., Antigua, St. Kitts, and Montserrat.

LEASK, J. T., M.B., Ch.M. (Edin.) 1879.—Col. surg., Malacca, Jan., 1891; ditto, Penang, Apr., 1893; ag. col. surg. res., Singapore, May, 1895, to Mar., 1896; ag. col. surg. Penang, Mar., 1896; col. surg. res., Singapore, Jan., 1897; ag. prim. civ. med. offr., S. S., Aug., 1902.

LE CAMP, CHARLES LOUIS THEODORE ADLER.—Ed. South African Coll.; passed Cape civ. ser. exam., Dec., 1888; apptd. to gov.'s staff on probation, Jan., 1889; on fixed estab. as 3rd-cl. clk., July, 1889; res. Cape serv. and apptd. to high comsnr.'s staff, Oct., 1890; 1st clk. to high comsnr., 1890; transf. to Bloemfontein as ch. clk. and regnr. to sec., O.R.C. Admintrn., Feb., 1901; ch. clk. to col. sec., O.R.C., June, 1902; clk. to ex. coun., June, 1902; ag. astt. col. sec., April to Aug., 1903.

LECLEZIO, SIR E. P. J., KNT. BACH. (1887), C.M.G. (1897).—B. 1832; called to the bar, Mid. Tem., 1858; graduate of the Faculty of Laws, Paris, 1858; ag. substitute procureur and advoc.-gen., Mauritius, in 1868, 1869, and 1870; mem. of the coun. of govt., 1869-1878; 1st puisne judge, 1879; ch. justice, 1883; ret., 1898.

LEE-JONES, JOHN WM.—Called to the Bar, Gray's Inn, 1903; astt. master, Queen's Coll., Hong Kong, Jan., 1885; ag. ch. clk. at the magistracy and clk. to the justices, Mar., 1894; ag. dep.-registrar and acctnt., sup. ct., Hong Kong, Sept., 1897; ag. dep.-registrar and appraiser, May, 1900; J.P., 1900; dep.-registrar and acctnt., sup. ct., June, 1902.

LEFEVRE, PHILIP LLEWELLYN.—Ed. at Victoria Coll., Jersey, and Brighton Coll., Sussex; clk., G.P.O., Cape Town, Feb., 1895; clk., atty.-gen.'s off., Feb., 1896; clk. to res. mag., Glen Grey, Feb., 1896; clk. to res. mag., East London, Sept., 1896; clk. sol.-gen.'s off., Grahamstown, Apr., 1899; clk., atty.-gen.'s off. (treason branch), Cape Town, Sept., 1900; B.A., Cape Univ., 1900; ch. clk. to atty.-gen., O.R.C., June, 1901.

LEFROY, GEORGE ANTHONY, A.M.I.C.E.—Asst. survr., W. Australia, 1879-80; priv. sec. to Sir J. H. Lefroy as admstr. of Tasmania; joined pub. wks. dept., Perak, 1882; ag. supt., pub. wks. and res. engrnr., Larut, 1885-7; ag. res. engrnr., Perak state rly., 1886-7; ch. survr. and in charge survey dept., 1887.

LEFROY, HON. HENRY B., C.M.G. (1903).—Elected M.L.A., W. Australia, 1892; re-elected, 1894 and 1897; min. of educn., May, 1897; min. of mines, May, 1898; ag. gen. for W. Australia in London, 1901; resigned, 1904.

LEGGE, C. A. S.—Clerical asst., B. Guiana, May, 1897; 6th class offr., cust., June, 1899; 5th class clk., pol. dept., Dec., 1900; lieut., B. G. Artillery, 1901.

LEGGE, CHAS. HENRY GLADMAN.—Clk. to the atty.-gen., Trinidad, Sept., 1867; 3rd clk. in the audit office, Apr., 1872; was clk. of the col. hosp., Port of Spain, Oct., 1873; 6th clk., rec-gen.'s dept., Nov., 1874; 2nd clk., audit office, Jan., 1875; ch. clk., patent office, 1880; 2nd clk., audit office, Demerara, May, 1880 (designation altered to "Inspr. of Accounts," Jan., 1881); ch. clk., Jan., 1882; ag. auditor-gen., 1883-6-8-9.

LE HUNTÉ, SIR GEORGE RUTHVEN, K.C.M.G. (1903), C.M.G. (1898).—B. 1852; Trin. Coll., Camb., 1873; M.A., 1880; called to the bar, Inner Tem., May, 1881; 2nd priv. sec. to gov., Fiji, 1875; stip. mag., 1875; res. comsnr., Colo Viti Levu, 1877; ag. comdt., A.N.C., 1878-9; ag. col. sec., 1880; astt. col. sec., Jan., 1882; ag. atty.-gen., Nov., 1883; judicial comsnr. for the high comsnr. to W. Pacific Is., May, 1883; ag. atty.-gen., May, 1884; ag. rec-gen., Jan., 1886; pres. of Dominica, 1887; col. sec., Barbados, with dormant comsnr. as admstr., 1894; col. sec. of Mauritius, 1897; lieut. govrn. of Br. New Guinea, 1898; gov. of S. Australia, 1903.

LEISK, JAMES RANKINE—Chartered acctnt., Glasgow; astt. recvr. of rev., Johannesburg, 22nd Sep., 1900; ch. clk. to cont. of treasry., Transvaal, 21st May, 1901; astt. sec. treasry., 1st Apr., 1902; sec. to treasry., 1st July, 1903; (Queen's S. African war medal with 3 clasps).

LE JUGE DE SEGRAIS, PAUL.—Assoc. M.I.C.E., govt. survr. and supt. of pub. wks., Seychelles, June, 1891; govt. engr. and archt., Mauritius, 14th Sept., 1896; ag. survr.-gen., 1896-97.

LE MESSURIER, H. W.—3rd landing waiter and astt. tide survr. of cust., Newfdld., 1894 to 1897; astt. collr. and sec. to bd. of rev., 1897; dep. min. of cust., with title of astt. collr., 1898 (commissariat clk. under astt. commissaries prior to the removal of the Imperial troops).

LEMIÈRE, H.—Dist. mag., Flaq., Nov., 1882, Dec., 1885, and Sept., 1897, Grand Port, June, 1884, and Sept., 1888, Moka, Jan., 1885, Port Louis, Feb., 1886, Pamplemousses, Dec., 1890, Plaines Wilhems (Rose Hill), Apr., 1896.
LEMON, ARTHUR HENRY.—Ed. at Merchant Taylors' Schl. and Exeter Coll., Oxford (scholar); B.A., 1887; cadet, Straits, 1888; priv. sec. to gov., Sept., 1889, to Jan., 1890; attached to Chinese protectorate, Penang, Aug., 1891; sec. to currency comte., June, 1893; ag. dist. offr., S. Malacca, Dec., 1893; passed in Malay, 1894; ag. 3rd mag., Singapore, Apr., 1894; ag. 2nd asst. col. sec., May, 1895; ag. asst. col. sec. and clk. of couns., June, ag. 2nd asst. col. sec., Aug., 1895; ag. dist. offr. Malacca, Oct., 1895; dist. offr. Prov. Wellesley, June, 1896, but continued to act at Malacca; ag. 2nd mag., Penang, July, 1898; ag. asst. P.M.G., Penang, Aug., 1898; 2nd asst. col. sec., Jan., 1902; ag. collr. of land rev. and reg. of deeds, Penang, April, 1903.

LENNOX, ARKILL NAPIER OLIVER.—Sixth clk., immigr. dept., Br. Guiana, 1882; 5th clk., 1884; 4th clk., 1885; awarded 2nd class certif. in Hindustani, 1885; acted as 1st clk., 1887, and July, 1889, to Jan., 1890; 3rd class clk., land dept., Jan., 1891; 2nd-class clk., Apr., 1891.

LEVEY, GEORGE COLLINS, C.M.G. (1878).—B.1835; mem. leg. coun., Victoria, 1861-8; was sec. to the Victorian comsn., and ag. comsnr. in charge of Victorian exhibits at Paris Exhibn., 1878; sec., Melbourne Exhibn., 1880-1; exec. comsnr., Victoria, Amsterdam Exhibn., 1883; sec., Adelaide Jubilee Exhibn., 1887, and Tasmanian Exhibn., 1894.

LE VIEUX, LEON.—Asst. survr., pub. wks. dep., Seychelles, 24th May, 1902.

LEWIS, ARTHUR KENNEDY.—Ed. at Wesleyan high schl. and C.M.S. grammar schl., S. Leone; med. dresser attached to Anglo-French boundary comsn., Dec., 1891 to Apl. 1892 (recd. thanks of govt.); clk. to D.C.; clk. of ct. of requests; registr. of births and deaths, W. dist., 1893 to 1895; 3rd clk. regiar.-gen.'s dept., 1895 to 1897; 2nd clk., atty.-gen.'s off., 1898; travelled with and clk. to atty.-gen. during trial of insurgents by Judge G. A. Bonner, 1898; transport clk., N.A. dept., 1899; ditto P. W. D., Jan., 1900 to July, 1901; offr. in charge of transport on govr.'s tours, 1899-1901; registr. offr., G.P.O., Freetown, Aug., 1901 to Jan., 1903; asst. postmr., Gambia, Feb., 1903.

LEWIS, E. CORNEWALL.—Entered Govt. office, St. Vincent, as supernum., May, 1877; clk. to Kingstown pol. mag., 1880; ag. col. regist., 1883; acted as provost-marshal, 1884; ag. col. postmr., 1885; ag. regist., 1886; dep. coroner, Kingstown, 1886; acctnt. of pub. wks. dept., Grenada, 1887; col. postmr., St. Vincent, 1889; ag. col. postmr., Grenada, Jan. to Mar., 1889; ag. regist. sup. court, St. Vincent, Nov., 1889, to Nov., 1890; ex officio inspr. of prisons, regist. of the vice-adm. court, ag. col. postmr., Grenada, Aug., 1891; resumed col. postmr., St. Vincent, Jan., 1892; J.P., 1892; asst. postmr.-gen., Hong Kong, 1899; J.P., 1899; ag. postmr.-gen., 1900, 1901, 1902, and 1903.

LEWIS, CAPT. E. H.—Joined 21st Lancers in India, 1892; present with that regt. at battle of Omdurman, 1898 (medal and Khedive's medal); served with W.A.F.F. from July, 1899, to May, 1903; served with expedn. for relief of Kumasi, 1900 (Ashanti medal); present at capture of Kontagoro, 1901 (ment. in despa., medal with clasp for N. Nigeria); present at capture of Kano (clasp for N. Nigeria) 1903; apptd. 3rd cls. res., N. Nigeria, May, 1903.

LEWIS, JOHN CHRISTOPHER.—Ent. Trinidad service, 1861; postmr., San Fernando, Sept., 1869; received the thanks of inhabitants for his services in 1882; ag. 2nd clk., G.P.O., 1868; ag. P.M.G., 1886 and 1891; comsnr. for affidavits and J. P.; received thanks of inhabitants of San Fernando in 1882 for his zeal in discharge of his duties, and the legis. coun. in Jan., 1893, passed a unanimous resolution that his long services were deserving of recognition.

LEWIS, JOHN E. A.—B.A., Caius Coll., Camb., 1883; extra offr., Sarawak civ. ser., Oct., 1886; mag., and manager Sarawak govt. printing off., Aug., 1888; ag. princ. insp. of pol. and prisons, Nov., 1889, to May, 1890; Sept., 1894, Dec., 1895; clk. to gen. coun., July, 1897; res., 2nd class, Sept., 1898.

LEWIS, JOHN PENRY.—Ed. at Mill Hill Schl. and Queen's Univ.; B.A., 1876; M.A., 1882; writer, Ceylon civ. ser., July, 1877; ag. pol. mag., Matare, Jan., 1881; ditto, Pet. Pedro, 1883; ag. office ast. to govt. agt., Jaffna, N.P., 1883; pol. mag., Gam-pula, 1884; ag. office ast. to govt. agt., cent. prov., Kandy, 1885; ag. comsnr. of requesta, Colombo, 1886-6; office ast. to govt. agent, C.P., 1887; ag. dist. judge, Matare, 1888; ast. agt., Negombo, 1891; ditto Vavuniya Vilan Kulam, Apr., 1896; ag. ast. govt. agt., Chilan, Apr., 1896; ag. dist. judge, Kurunegala, June; Negombo, Sept., 1896; special offr. under waste lands ordnec. No. 1 of 1897; ag. govt. agt., N. prov., 19th May, 1902; ditto, Cent. prov., 7th Nov., 1902; ditto, N. prov., 13th June, 1903.

LEWIS, HON. SR NEIL ELLIOT, K.C.M.G. (1902), C.M.G. (1901), B.A.—B.1858; atty.-gen. in Dobson-Hervy ministry, Tasmania, 1892-4; premier and atty.-gen. in Lewis ministry, 1900; joined lat Commonwealth ministry as min. without portfolio, Jan., 1901.

LEWIS, SR WALTER LLEWELLYN, KT. BACh. (1904) M.A.—Gold Medallist, Queen's Univ. (Ireland), 1869 and 1871; called to the bar, Md. Tem., Jan., 1876; South Wales and Chester circuits; stip. justice, Trinidad, Jan., 1883; chmn. of coman. on agricultural contracts; chmn. of directors, public service widows' and orphan fund, 1890-1900; puisne judge, 1893; ch. justice, British Honduras, 1900.

LEY, ANDREW K.—Priv. sec. to gov. Labuan, 1882; ag. col. treas. and auditor, 1882 to 1885, and judge gen. ct., 1884-5; mag., ct. of requests, and P.M.G. Sarawak, Oct., 1886; also shipping master and coroner, 1st div.

LEYS, PETER, C.M.G. (1890).—B.1851; ed. at Univa. of Glasgow and Edinburgh, of which latter he is a graduate in medicine; entered col. service, Labuan, Feb., 1876; adminstd. the govt. 1881-7; held a coman. as H.B.M.'s consul-gen. for Borneo; ret., 1889.

LIGHTBOURN, JAMES THOMAS.—Ed. at Bahamas collegiate institute; supernumerary, treasy. and cust. dept., Bahamas, Jan., 1885; 3rd clk., treasy., Dec., 1885; 2nd clk. and bookkeeper, treasy. dept., 1895; has held several acting appointments.

LINCOLN, GABRIEL.—Copyist, col. sec.'s off., Mauritius, 24th June, 1884; clk. to ex. coun. and coun. of govt., 1st June, 1901; ch. clk., col. sec.'s off., 9th Nov., 1903.

LINDER, CONRAD.—Served under late O.F.S. govt. as postmr. and J.P. at Wepener, 1873; resident J.P. at Wepener, 1874; landdrost's clk. at Bethulie, 1878; govt. claim inspr., Oliphantston-tein, 1880; landdrost, Boeshof, 1882; regist. of deeds, 1894; receiver of rev., Bloemfontein, O.R.C., Apl., 1900; regist. of deeds, Mar., 1901.

LINLITHGOW, 1ST MARQUIS OF (U.K. creat. 1902), 7TH EARL OF HOFETOUP (Soot.), P.C., K.T. (1900), G.C.M.G. 1889), G.C.V.O. (1900).

JOHN ADRIAN LOUIS HOPE; also VISCOUNT
AITHRIE and BARON HOFF (1703, Scotch peerages); BARON HOPETOUN (1809) and BARON NIDDRY (1814) in peerage of U.K.—B. 1860; lieut., Lanark Yeom. Cav. 1859; lord-in-waiting, 1886-6 and 1888-9; lord high comsnr. to gen. assem. of Church of Scotland, 1887-8; gov., Victoria, 1889-95; paymr.-gen., 1895; Lord Chamberlain, 1899; governor-general and commander-in-chief of the Commonwealth of Australia, 1900; resigned, 1902.

LISTER, JOSEPH STORR, L.S.O. (1903).—Asst. to man. of Tukva tea and cinchona estate, Darjeeling, May, 1870; passed lower standard exam. in Hindustani and an exam. in land surveying and levelling; apptd. to the forest dept., Punjab, in charge of Changa Manga, Lahore, and Umballa plantations, 1871; transfd. to Hazara, to assist dep. conservator in exploring and reporting on hill forests of Khagan; on special duty to Kulu and Kangra in charge of Nurpur sub-division; left India owing to ill-health, 1874; supt. of plantations, Cape, Jan., 1875; J.P. and road mag., Aug., 1875; in conjunction with other duties, custodian of ex-chief Langalibalele and ex-king Cetewayo during their detention at Uitvlugt and Oude Molen; established plantations at Worcester, Beaufort West, Tokai, and Kluitjes Kraal; sec. to sub-committee, for wood and vegetable products, Indian and Col. Exhib., 1886; conservator of forests, E. diva., Sept., 1888.

LLEWELYN, Sir ROFT B., K.C.M.G. (1898), C.M.G. (1889).—B. 1845; extra clk., C.O., London, from 1868; regis. in col. sec.'s office, Jamaica, Nov., 1869; was nominated as one of a comsnr. apptd. to inquire into prison discipline in Jamaica, 1873; priv. sec. to Sir J. P. Grant, July, 1873; clk. of priv. coun., Jamaica, 1877; comsnr. for Turks Is., 1878; admstr. of Tobago, 1885, admstr., St. Vincent, 1888; ag. admstr., Grenada, 1888; admstr., St. Lucia, 1889, with dormant comsnr. as admstr., Windward Is.; admstr., Gambia, 1891; African war medal with two clasps, 1891-2, and 1893-4; gov. Windward Islands, Oct., 1900.

LOYD, AUGUSTUS GEORGE.—Ch. clk. and cashier, col. treas., S. Leone, Dec., 1896; ag. col. treas., Apr. to July, 1899; ag. asst. col. treas., July, 1899.

LOYD, JAMES S.—Ed. at Codrington Coll., Barbados; apptd. to 3rd clerkship, customs, Barbados, Nov., 1876; 2nd indoor offr., customs, Dec., 1890.

LOCKE, R. F.—Apptd. cons. agt. in Oil Rivers (now S. Nigeria) Protec., July, 1892; ag. v.-cons. and dep. comsnr., Benin river, May to Nov., 1894; Brohemie expdn., 1894, mentd. in Adml. Bedford's desps., med. and clasp; apptd. dist. comsnr., Apr., 1896; ag. v.-cons. and dep. comsnr., Warri, Sapele, and Benin Riv. Dista., May to Dec., 1896; one of two survivors Benin massacre, Jan., 1897; apptd. dep. comsnr. and v.-cons., Apr., 1897; now divisi. comsnr., West Div., S. Niger Protec.

LOCKHART, J. H. STEWART, C.M.G. (1898); F.R.G.S., M.R.A.S.—B. 1858; Edin. Univ.; Greek medallist, etc.; apptd., after compet. exam., to a Hong Kong cadetship, 1878; attached to the C.O. for one year, 1879; passed cadet, 1882; supt. opium revenue, Mar., 1883; asst. col. sec. and asst. auditor-gen., Aug., 1883; ag. regis. gen., 1884 and 1885; regis.-gen., 1887, and M.L.C., 1889; mem. exec. coun., 1891; chairmn. bd. of examiners in Chinese, 1891; ditto govrmg. body Queen's Coll., 1894; ag. col. sec., Apr., 1894; col. sec. and regis.-gen., Mar., 1895; special comsnr. to report on the extension of the bndry. of H. Kong, 1898; representative of Gt. Br. to delimitate bndry., for both of which reed. thanks of S.S., 1899; rector of coll. of medicine for Chinese, 1895-1902; comsnr. of Weihaiei, 1902.

LOCKHART, NORMAN.—Fourth revenue offr., Dominica, Feb., 1880; ag. postmr., 1881; ag. excise offr., May, 1882; 3rd revenue offr., 1883; quarantine offr., 1886; ag. mag., Nevis, 1891; ditto, Dist. E., Dominica, 1892, 1895, 1896; mag., Anguilla, 1896; ag. mag., Dominica, 1897; asst. treas. and regis. of shipping, St. Kitts-Nevis, 1897; ag. treas., 1899, 1900, 1901, and 1902. treas., Grenada, 1903.

LOCKYER, E.—Examr. of accts., audit dept., O.R.C., 26th June, 1903.

LONG, THOMAS.—Topographical survr. in the survr.-gen.'s office, Newfild., Mar., 1872; 1st clk., Sept., 1882; dep. min. agricul. and mines, 1898.

LONGLEY, HON. J. WILBERFORCE.—B.A., Acadia Coll., N. Scotia, 1871; M.A., 1875; called to the bar, N.S., Sept., 1875; comsnr. sup. ct., 1876; elected to Prov. Parlmt., June, 1882; sworn in mem. of exec., July, 1884; atty.-gen., May, 1886; comsnr. for revising and consolidating the law and framing Judicature Act, Oct., 1882; editorial writer "Acadian Recorder" since 1873.

LORANGER, L. O., K.C.—Atty.-gen., prov. of Quebec, Canada; apptd. a judge of sup. ct. of Quebec, 1882.

LORANS, HENRI, M.B.C.M., and D.P.H., Edin.—Police and prison surg., Mauritius, 1884; poor law med. offr., Port Louis, 10th Jan., 1884; med. inspr., 15th Nov., 1895; ag. diretr., med. and health dept., 1900 and 1902; nom. mem. of coun. of govt.

LORNIE, J., M.A., B.Sc. Edin.—Cadet, S. S., Nov., 1899; passed final exam. in Malay, Apr., 1901; ag. head of Malay Coll., Malacca, May, 1901; ag. asst. regis., sup. ct., and mag. and sheriff, Malacca, Apl., 1903; ag. dist. offr., Penang, Jan., 1904.

LOVEGROVE, CHARLES ARTHUR, A.M.I.C.E.—Ed. Charterhouse; asst. to Mr. W. Wilson, C.E., Westminster, 1879; contractor's engrn., Coleford and Monmouth rlyv., 1881; asst. to Mr. W. Wilson, C.E., 1884; dist. engrn., P.W.D., Ceylon, 1886; ag. prov. engrn., W. Prov., 1897; ditto, N.W. Prov., 1897; ditto, S. Prov., and mem. mun. coun., Galle, 1898; ag. prov. engrn., E. Prov., 1898; ag. asst. dir. of pub. wks., Ceylon, 1900; prov. engrn., Uva, 1900; asst. dir., P.W., 1903.

LOVELL, SIR FRANCIS HENRY, KT. BACH. (1900), C.M.G. (1893).—B. 1844; col. surg., S. Leone, Dec., 1873; med. offr., imigrn. dept., Mauritius, 1878; ch. med. offr. and pres. gen. bd. of health, 1879; mem. coun. of govt., 1885; surg.-gen. and med. offr. of health, and mem. legis. coun., Trinidad, Sept., 1893-1901; also mem. exec. coun., 1894; ret., 1902.

LOW, ALFRED M.—Ed. at Aldenham; open scholarship at Pem. Coll., Camb., 1890; B.A. class. tripos, 1893; ag. prof. of classics, Codrington Coll., Barbados, 1896; 3rd master, Queen's Roy. Coll., Trinidad, June, 1897.

LOW, SIR HUGH, G.C.M.G. (1889), K.C.M.G. (1883), C.M.G. (1879).—B. 1824; sec. to gov't. of Labuan, 1848; pol. mag., 1850; admnstr. the govt. of Labuan five times between 1885 and 1876; Br. ree., Perak, 1877; negotiated treaty of Protection with Sultan of Brunei, 1888; ret., 1889.

LUCAS, CHARLES PRESTWOOD, C.B. (1901), B.A.—B.1863; ed. at Winchester Coll., and Balliol Coll., Oxford; open exhibitioner; 1st class in mods., 1873,
and 1st class in final classical schools, June, 1876; Chancellor's prize for Latin essay, 1877; called to the bar by the Soc. of Lincoln's Inn, Easter, 1885; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. in the office of the sec. of state for the cols., Apr., 1877; priv. sec. to Sir R. Herbert, Dec., 1881; Earl Granville, Feb., 1886, and again to Sir R. Herbert, Aug., 1886; also chairman of comttee. of emigrants information office till 31st Dec., 1896; 1st class clk., Feb., 1892; author of "Historical Geography of the British Colonies"; prin. clk., Sept., 1896; asst. under-sec. of state, June, 1897.

LUCIE-SMITH, A. VAN W.—Ed. at Rugby; solr., Br. Guiana, 1877; called to bar, Mid. Tem., 1881; ag. solr.-gen., Br. Guiana, 1882 to 1887; pres. dist. ct., Famagusta, Cyprus, 1887; Limasol, 1892; ag. Queen's advoc., 1893; ag. judge, cons. ct., Constantinople, 1896; res. mag., Kingston, Jamaica, Nov., 1896; puisne judge, B.G., Jan., 1898; ag. ch. justice, 1900-01; one of the compilers of the "Rules of Court," 1900.

LUCKIE, D.M., F.S.S.—Trained in a lawyer's office in Montrose, Scotland; in 1862 emigrated to N. Zealand, as editor and part proprietor of the "Nelson Colonist," which he largely popularised; in 1872 was elected mem. of parl. for Nelson City; in 1873 became editor of the "Southern Cross, and when it was amalgamated with the "New Zealand Herald," the leading journal in the col., became ch. editor of the combined papers; asst. comsnr. of govt. assurance, 1878.

LUGARD, BRIG.-GEN. SIR F. D., K.C.M.G. (1901), C.B. (1895), D.S.O.—B. 1858; ed. Rossall and Sandhurst; 1st comn., 9th foot, May, 1878; capt., Aug., 1885; major, Aug., 1896; temp. col., 1898; to India, Sept., 1878 active service, Afghanistan, Sept., 1879-80; medal, Soudan, Feb. to Nov., 1885; medal, clasp, "Tofrek" Khedive's Star; despatched to Birmah, Oct., 1886, to Aug., 1887; mentioned in despatches, D.S.O. and medal. To Africa, Feb., 1888; commanding expdn. against slave traders; very severely wounded. To East Africa, Nov., 1889; exploration of Sabakh; admnstd. Uganda; wrote "Our East African Empire." July, 1894, went to Borgu in comd. expedition, and made treaties; hit by arrow, returned, Apr., 1895; Feb., 1896, led expedition across Kalashari for Br. Charterland Co.; apptd. comn., and comdt., West African frontier force, Aug., 1897; went out Mar., 1898; high comn. for Northern Nigeria, 29th Dec., 1899.

LUMB, CHARLES FREDERICK.—Ed. at Liverpool Inst. (Yates exhibitioner), and Downing Coll., ('sch. (scholar and prizeman in maths, nat. sci., and law); B.A., math. tripes, 1870; M.A., and LL.M., 1877; LL.D., 1892; barrister of Linc.'s Inn, 1874, and practised on N. circuit; vice-pres. of Liverpool inst., and mem. of Liverpool schl. bd.; prosecutor for the mint, Feb., 1886; 2nd puisne judge, Trinidad, 1887; mem. educn. comn., 1887; of bd. of educn., 1887; of Roy. Coll. coun., 1888; of library comn., 1889; drafted dist. cts. and educn. ordinances and rules thereunder; puisne judge, Jamaica, 1892; mem. of bd. of educn., 1893-4; ag. ch. justice, 1895-6; chmn. of the education comn., 1897-8.

LUSCOMBE, CAPT. G. A.—Local comdt. of pol., Cyprus, 1898.

LUSHINGTON, CHARLES MORANT.—Ceylon writer, 1876; mag., 1878; asst. to govt. agt. N.W. prov., 1883; dist. judge, Kegalla, Mar., 1889; ditto, Ratnapura, July, 1889; ag. asst. govt. agt., Negombo, Oct., 1890; at N'Ellya, 1892; at Matale, 1894; at N'Ellya, 1895; at Trincomalee, 1896; ag. govt. agt., E. prov., 13th June, 1903.

LYNCH, G. W. A.—Ed. at Westminster, Genville and Caius Coll., Camb. (B.A., 1883), and St. Thomas's hospital, Lond.; M.R.C.S. Eng.; L.R.C.P. Lond., 1885; M.B., B.C., Camb., 1886; govt. med. offr., Fiji, 1890; sen. med. offr., 1898; ag. ch. med. offr., Oct., 1899, to Jan., 1900; ditto, and ag. agt.-gen. for immigr., Mar., 1903, to Jan., 1904.

LYNE, SIR WILLIAM JOHN, K.C.M.G. (1900).—B. 1844; elected to N. Wales parlmt., 1880; sec. pub. wks., 1885-7, and again 1891; mem. exec. coun.; prim. and col. treas., Sept., 1899; joined first Commonwealth ministry as min. of state for home aff., Jan., 1901.

LYONS, CAPT. F. W.—Ed. at Portarlington school, and Trin. Coll., Dublin; joined 80th regt. as 2nd lieut., 15th Feb., 1878; capt., 1884; adjutant, 1885; adjut. of volunteers, 1887-90; capt. reserve of officers, 1890; ag. asst. sup. of pol., S.S., 5th Mar., 1891, to 31st Mar., 1893; apptd. asst. comn., Perak Sikhs, 1st Apr., 1893; acted as capt., sup. of pol., and prisons, Selangor, Aug., 1893, to Feb., 1895; served in S. Africa, 1878-80, medal with clasp; served in Soudan, 1886-86, medal and Khedive's Star; served in Pahang during disturbances, and recd. thanks of S. of S., 1894; acted as chief pol. offr., Perak, 1900-2; apptd. deputy sup. of pol., Hong Kong, 7th Sept., 1902; ag. capt. sup. of pol., etc., 1903-4.

LYTTELTON, RT. HON. ALFRED, P.C., M.A., Camb.; Hon. M.A., Oxford; K.C.—B. 1857; ed. at Eton, and Trin. Coll., Camb.; barrister: bencher, Inner Tem., 1899; legal priv. sec. to Sir H. James, attorney-gen., 1882 to 1886; recorder of Hereford, 1894; recorder of Oxford, 1895; dep. high steward of Univ. of Camb., 1899; M.P. for Leamington, Warwick, 1895; chmn. of Transvaal concessions comn., S. Africa, 1900-1; apptd. by Newfd. govt. as arbitrator in case of the Reid railway contract, 1902; S. of S. for the colonies, Oct., 1903.

MAASDORP, CHRISTIAN GEORGE.—Atty.-gen., Transvaal, Sept., 1878; resign., Jan., 1880; puisne judge, sup. ct., Cape, Nov., 1885; Superiorct., Cape Town, 1896.

McALLISTER, ANDREW.—Asst. survr., Oi Rivers Prot. (now So. Nigeria), Sept., 1892; ag. survr.-gen., Feb. to Oct., 1894, and Aug., 1897, to Dec., 1898; survr.-gen., Jan., 1899; dir. of pub. wks., Jan., 1900.

MACARTHUR, MALCOLM STEWART H.—Ed. Queen's Coll., Oxford; cadet S. Stiltns., Nov., 1895; ag. dep. registr. of deeds, Penang, 1896; passed final exam. in Malay, Apr., 1897; ag. priv. sec. to gov., S.S., Jan., 1897; ag. dist. offr., Balik Pulau, Aug., 1897; and 3rd mag., Penang, 1898; ag. 2nd astt. col. sec., Apr., 1899; ag. astt. sec. to gov't. Selangor, Apr., 1900, to Jan., 1901; dist. offr., Penang, Jan., 1901; ag. 2nd astt. col. sec., Jan. to May, 1901; ag. collector of land rev. and registr. of deeds, Sing.; also ag. sec. to high comn. of F.M.S., May, 1902; ag. comn. of ct. of requests, Sing., Aug., 1903; astt. supt. of Indian immigts, in addition to other duties, 13th Nov., 1903; ag. 2nd astt. col. sec., Nov., 1903; confirmed, July, 1904; seconded for spec. serv. under F.O. in Brunei, Apr., 1904.

MACARTHUR, WM. HENRY, M.R.C.V.S.—Govt. vet. surgeon, Penang, S. Stiltns., 21st May, 1892.

MACASKIE, JOHN COCHRANE.—Pres. dist. ct., Cyprus, 1895.

MACAULAY, JOHN DAVIDSON.—Extra clk. col. sec.'s office, S. Leone, 1874; in customs, 1875; tide waiter, 1877; landing waiter, 1879; clk. of customs, 1883.
MACBRIDE, ROBERT KNOX, C.M.G. (1890).—B. 1844; suptg. offr., pub. wks. dept., Ceylon, 1866; irrigation asst., 1872; prov. asst., N.-Cent. prov., 1874; ditto, Uva, 1876; S. prov., 1878; and Cent. prov., 1882; dir. of pub. wks., Oct., 1885.

McCALL, GEO. H.—Ed. at Queen's Roy. Coll., Trinidad; ag. sub-collr., No. 4 dist., Tobago, Aug., 1895; clk. to comsnr. financial bd. and bd. of educn., Jan., 1896; asst. clk. to warden during expenditure of loan, Oct., 1896; ag. postmtr., Dec., 1896; clk. to comsnr. financial and educn. bds. and asst. clk. to warden, Jan., 1897; twice ag. harbourmr., excise offr., and landing waiter, Tobago, 1898; landing waiter and clk. treasry., Jan., 1899; transf. to cust., Trinidad, Feb., 1899; cust. offr., July, 1899.

McCALLUM, COLONEL SIR HENRY EDWARD, R.E., G.C.M.G. (1904), K.C.M.G. (1898), C.M.G. (1887), A.D.C. to the Queen (1900).—B. 1852; entered the Roy. Mil. Acad., Woolwich, July, 1869; passed first out of 52 cadets, 1871; after two years' practical training at Chatham, proceeded to Portsmouth (1874), and apptd. supt. of telegraphy, S. dist.; transf. to office of inspr.-gen. of fortifications; priv. sec. to gov. S. Settlements, Sir William Jervois, and attended him on various missions to the native states of the Malay Peninsula; mentioned in despatches for the assistance given in preparing a project for the defence of Singapore, and again in Dec., 1876, for services in connection with Perak comsh. of inquiry; suptg. engnr. admiralty works, Hong Kong, Apr., 1877; in Apr., 1878, selected to proceed to Singapore to adopt measures for the defence of that port; attached to the office of inspr. of wks., roy. arsenal, July, 1879, to July, 1880, when apptd. dep. col. engnr., S. Sttlmts.; is a Pollock medalist of 1871; the annual Fowke medallist for 1874; is an assoc. of instt. of civ. engnr., etc.; col. engnr. and survr.-gen., S. Sttlmts., 1884; men. of the exec. and legis. couns.; pres. Singapore municipality, Feb., 1881, to July, 1886; apptd. to construct new fortifications of Singapore, Mar., 1885; comdt. Singapore volr. art., 1888; special comsnr. in Pahang during disturbances, 1891; received thanks of S. of S.; gov. Lagos, 1897; gov. of Newfoundland, 1898; gov. of Natal, 1901.

McCarthy, James A.—Inner Temple common law scholarship, 1878; called to the bar, Jan., 1879; Queen's advoc., S. Leone, Apr., 1890; also admiralty advoc., mem. exec. and legis. couns., and bd. of educn.; accompanied admstr. to Monrovia in 1892, and to Port Lokkokh in 1893; acted several times as registr.-gen. since 1889; ag. ch. just., May to Sept., 1893; escheator, 1893; sol.-gen., G. Coast, June, 1895.

McCarthy, Robt. Henry.—2nd class clk. impl. customs, Belfast, Feb., 1875; served at Cork and Plymouth; selected for special service with survrs. gen., and in connection with reorganisation of customs statistical dept., 1893; 2nd offr., Folkestone, 1894; collr. of customs, Trinidad, Dec., 1895; mem. leg. coun., 1898; one of the representatives of Trinidad at commercial conferences at Washington and Ottawa, 1900; apptd. to ex. coun. 1903; del. for Trinidad at W. Indian quarantine confe., 1904.

McCay, Lt.-COL. THE HON. J. W.—M.A., LL.M.; mem. leg. ass., Victoria, Nov., 1895, and Oct., 1897, to Dec., 1899; min. of pub. instrn. and comsnr. of trade and cust., Dec., 1899, to Jan., 1900; mem. of Commonwealth parl., Mar., 1901, and Dec., 1893; min. for defence, ditto, Oct., 1904.

Macconnal, W. G.—Apptd. ast. acctnt., refugee camps, O.R.C., 24th April, 1902; auditor, refugee camps' accts., attached to audit dept., 30th Sept., 1902; 2nd examr. of accts, audit dept., 1st Dec., 1902; clk., treasry., 1st May, 1903.

McCord, Neville Wm.—5th excise offr., B. Hond., Oct., 1893; 4th ditto, Nov., 1895; 2nd cust. offr., Nov., 1900; 1st excise offr., June, 1902; 1st grade cust. and ex. offr., Aug., 1903.

McCowen, John R.—L.S.O. (1903), A.D.C., J.P.—B. 1844; served 9 years in R.I. constab.; apptd. to Newfd. constab., 1871; inspr.-gen., 1895; recd. thanks of govt. on 5 occasions for spec. serv.; R.H.S. medal and thanks of govt. for saving life, 1878; gov., penitentiary, 1879; mem. of bd. of health, 1890; hon. sec., fire relief comm., 1892, and spec. thanked for serv.; chrmn., fire comsnr., 1893; spec. medal, 1897, and thanked by govt. for exceptional bravery at a fire; A.D.C. to govr., 1901.

McCulloch, Hon. Wm.—M.L.C. for Gippsland, Victoria; minister of defence, and vice-president of bd. of land and works, 1895-1899; min. of defence, 1901-2; ag. agent-general in London, 1902.

Macdonald, The Hon. Andrew Archibald.—Born at Three Rivers, Prince Edward's Is., 1829; a mem. of prov. assem., 1854 to 1860, and of the legis. coun. from 1863, when it became elective, until July, 1873, when he resig. seat in the legis. and exec. couns., and became prov. postm.-gen., until 1844, when apptd. lieut.-gov. of the prov., which position he occupied until Sept., 1899; was a deleg. to the Charlottetown and Quebec confe. in 1864, which settled the terms of union for the Dominion of Canada; called to the Senate of the Dominion, May, 1891.

McDonald, Ernest E.—Ed. Sydenham Coll., Kent; supernum. clk., col. sec.'s office, Br. Honduras, 1887; clk. to atty.-gen., Feb., 1888; clk., col. engnr.'s dept., Sept., 1888; 2nd clk., col. sec.'s office, June, 1892; ag. dist. comsnr. The Cay, Apr., 1895; Stan Creek, Mar., 1896; ch. clk., col. sec.'s office, Cyprus, Apr., 1897.

McDonald, Hon. James, K.C.—Called to the bar of Nova Scotia, 1851; created a Q.C., 1867; chief rly. comsnr. of N.S., from June, 1863, to Dec., 1864; one of the comsrs. (representing N.S.) to open trade relations between W. Indies, Mexico, Brazil, and the B.N.A. provs., 1865-66; sworn of the privy coun. of Canada, Oct., 1878, and apptd. min. of just. of Canada; sat in N.S. assem. from 1859 until 1867, and from 1871 until July, 1872, when returned to the house of commons; ch. just. of N.S.; joint comsnr. to inquire into charges agst. atty.-gen. of Jamaica, Dec., 1893.

Macdonald, John Alex.—Ed. High School, Inverness; law clk., 1896-1900; joined service co. Cameron Hdrs., 1900, and served in S. African campaign; clk., G.P.O., Bloemfontein, Nov., 1900; clk. to crown prosecutor, O.R.C., July, 1901; clk., sec. O.R.C. admin., Oct., 1901; clk. to col. sec., June, 1902.

McDonnell, John.—Ck. in the immigr. office of N. S. Wales in 1854; promoted in 1856; sen. clk. to the registr.-gen.; placed in charge of the compilation of the gen. statistics of the col. in 1858; sec. of the pol. dept. of Queensland on its separation from N.S.W., Feb., 1860; immigr. agt., Jan., 1866, inspr. of benevolent asylum and orphanages, also visiting justice to H.M.'s gaol and lun. asyl.; as well as ch. inspr. of distilleries; under-sec. and permanent head of the post and
telegraph dept. in 1870; major-commdt. of the Queensland vol. forces, 1877; lieut.-col. commdt. in 1878; ret., Nov., 1879, and placed on the staff with his rank as lieut.-col.; ag. commdt. of the defence forces in Feb., 1883, to 1884; mem. of immigr bd. since 1865.

MACDOUGALL, JOHN LORNE, C.M.G. (1897).—B. 1838; Auditor-gen. of Canada, Aug., 1878.

McDOUGALL, JOSEPH EASTON.—Son of Wm. McDougall, C.B.; ed. U.C. Coll.; called to bar, Feb., 1870; lecturer on criminal law and torts to law society of Ontario, 1879-83; Q.C. 1883; jun. judge ct. st. York, Mar., 1883; sen. judge, Sept., 1885; judge maritime ct., Ontario, Sept., 1885; chmn. of pol. bd. for Toronto, 1886.

MACDOUGALL, THE HON. WILLIAM, C.B. (1867).—Ed. at Victoria Univ., Cobourg; admitted an atty., Upper Canada, 1847; called to the bar, Hilary, 1862; founded (1848) the “Canada Farmer,” subsequently merged in the “Canadian Agriculturist,” which he published and edited until 1858; founded (1850) the “North American,” a Reform newspaper, of which he was chief editor until merged in the Toronto “Daily Globe” in 1857; leading political writer on the “Daily Globe,” from 1857 to 1860; represented Canada at the New York Exhibn., 1853; sec. of the Constitutional Reform Assoc. of Upper Canada, 1859; mem. of the exec. coun. and commr. of crown lands, Canada, May, 1862, to Mar., 1864; prov. sec. from June, 1864, and ag. min. of marine from July, 1866, until the union of the provinces, 1867; sworn of the Queen’s privy coun. in Canada; min. of pub. wks. for the Dominion from July, 1867; lieut.-gov. of Rupert’s Land and the N.W. territories, Oct., 1869; chmn. of the coun. to open trade relations with the W. Indies, Mexico, and Brazil, 1865-6; deleg. to the Charlottetown Union confce., 1864; to that at Quebec in the same year; and to the col. confce. in London to complete terms of union of B.N.A. cols., 1866-7; deleg. to England, with late Sir G. E. Cartier, to confer with imperial authorities on the defences of the Dominion, and for the acquisition of the N.W. territory, 1868; commr. for Ontario, for the settlement of N.W. boundary of the prov., 1871; sent to England by Dominion govt., 1873, as special commr. to confer with imperial govt. on subject of fisheries; returned to Canadian legislature in 1858, where he sat until the union of 1867, when returned to house of commons; elected to Ontario assem. in May, 1875; resig. Sept., 1878, and again returned to house of commons; ret. from public life, 1882, and resumed practice of his profession in Ottawa. Is a K.C.

McDOWELL, DONALD KEITH, C. M. G. (1901).—Prin. med. offr. of W.A.F.F.; accompanied Ashanti expdn., 1900, in that capacity; prin. civ. med. offr., Straits Settlements, Mar., 1903.

McEWAN, THOS. SMITH.—Assoc. M.I.C.E.; asst. construction engrn., Cape govt. rlyws., 1874; maintenance engrn., 1877; dist. engrn., 1880; res. engrn., Bethulie junction, Jan., 1891; East London, 1st Jan., 1893; Port Elizabeth, 1st May, 1894; res. engrn., western system, and dist. engrn., Dist. No. 1, 13th July, 1896; res. engrn., Cape Town, 1st July, 1897; ch. res. engrn., Port Elizabeth, 1st Apr., 1899; asst. engrn.-in-chief, 15th Mar., 1901; asst. gen. man. of rlyws., 16th May, 1901; gen. man., 12th Aug., 1902.

MACFARLANE, WM. HOULSWORTH, M.B., Ch. B.—Supt. and med. offr., hosp. for insane, New Norfolk, Tasmania, Oct., 1880.

McGEE, JOHN J.—Ed. at St. Peter’s Coll., Waterford, affiliated with the Catholic Univ., Dublin; was medallist in physical science; employed by the govt. of Canada on special service in dist. of Algoma, and on various surveys; subsequently professionally engaged under the Dominion govt. in the construction of the inter-colonial rly., and in connection with the rly. coun. of the house of commons; 1st class clk. in charge of survey branch of Dominion lands, Dept. of the Interior, 1879; clk. of the privy coun., Canada, May, 1882.

McGOWAN, JAMES.—B.A., Lond., and fellow of the Inst. of Actuaries, Lond.; acted as exam. to that inst., and engaged for many years in life assurance business; govt. actuary, Cape, 1890.

MacGREGOR, D. S.—Fellow of soc. of accnts. and auditors; ch. audit clk., Leeward, Apr., 1895; federal accnt., Jan., 1896; ag. treasr., St. Kitts-Nevis, Dec., 1896; ag. aud.-gen. and mem. of Leewards and Antigua leg. couns. and Antigua exec. coun., Sept., 1897, to Jan., 1898; on special mission to investigate and adjust accnts. of Trinidad, Dec., 1899, to May, 1900; auditor, British Honduras, June, 1900; ag. reg.-gen. and reg. of sup. ct. on two occasions in 1904.

McGREGOR, JAMES COMYN.—2nd lieut. 7th battn. K.R.R., 1881; lieut., 1891; sub-instr. Basutoland mtd. pol., 1884; asst. commr., 1893.

MacGREGOR, SIR WILLIAM, K.C.M.G. (1899), C.M.G. (1881), C.B. (1897).—B. 1847; ed. at Aberdeen, Glasgow, Berlin, and Paris; M.B., Abdn., 1872; M.D., 1874; Watson gold medallist, 1872; formerly res. surg. and res. physician, Glasgow Roy. Infirmary; res. physician, Roy. Lun. Asyl., Aberdeen; asst. govt. med. offr., Seychelles, 1873; supt., lun. asyl., and res. surg., Civil Hosp., Port Louis Mauritius, 1874; ch. med. offr., Fiji, Mar., 1875; also receiver-gen., and mem. of the exec. and legis. couns., Jan., 1877; has acted as regisr.-gen., agt. gen. of immigr., and commr. of lands; engaged, 1876, in the suppression of the disturbances in the mountains of Viti Levu, for which he was voted a gratuity of 200L; joint commr., 1877, for the settlement of debts due from natives and Europeans, and for the settlement of all pecuniary claims against the late govt. of Fiji; mem. of the Native Regulation Board, 1877; proceeded to Tonga, 1879, to report on the financial condition of that country; ag. col. sec., Nov., 1883, to June, 1884, and Oct., 1874, to Jan., 1875; admstr. of the govt., and ag. high commr. and consul-gen. for the W. Pacific, Jan. to Aug., 1875; representative of Fiji at the first session of the Fed. Coun. of Australasia, at Hobart, Jan., 1885; Albert medal of the 2nd class (1884), with the Clarke gold medal of the Roy. Hum. Soc. of Australasia in 1885, for saving life at sea; dep. admstr. of Fiji, Sept., 1885, and Aug., 1886; admstr. Br. New Guinea, 1888; lieut.-gov., 1895; gov. Lagos, 1899; gov., Newfoundland, 23rd July, 1904.

McGUIRE, WM.—Appkd., after open compet. clk. in the lower div. of the civ. serv., and assigned to the audit office, Nov., 1884; transf. to valuation office, Ireland, Nov., 1890, and to C.O., June, 1891; temp. staff officer, 1903.

MACINTYRE, D. C.—Harbour-master, Penang. S. Settmts., Sep., 1903.

McINTYRE, JOHN.—Apptd. puisne judge, Tasmania, 1899.

McINTYRE, PETER ADOLPHUS, M.D.—Lieut. govt., Prince Edward Island, Canada, 23rd May, 1899.

McINNIS, Lieut.-Col. EDWARD BOWATER (late 9th Lancers), C.M.G. (1890).—B. 1847; entd. army, 1865; adjt. 9th Lancers for several years, including
campaigns of 1878-9-80; Khyber Passa, under Lt.-Gen. Sir F. Maude, K.C.B., 1878; actions of Dei Khazi Killa, Dec., 1879; Siah Sung, Dec., 1879; others at Kabul; siege of Sherpur under Lt.-Gen. Sir F. Roberts, K.C.B.; with the 9th Lancers on the march from Kabul to Kandahar; at battle of Mazra (Kandahar), Sept., 1880; twice mentd. in despatches; bronze star, med. and two clasps; inspr.-gen., G. Coast constab., Mar., 1887; mentd. in despatches by Sir R. B. Griffith, K.C.M.G.; comdt. local forces, Trinidad, June, 1890; mem. exec. coun., Sept., 1890; inspr.-gen. of Br. Guiana pol., May, 1891; comdt. Br. Guiana militia, Nov., 1892, with rank of col.; on special duty to Uruan on Venezuelan frontier, Jan., 1896; commanded cavalry of the colonial contingent at H.M.'s Diamond Jubilee, June, 1897; ret., 1902.

MACKAY, G.—M.A., Aberdeen, asst. master, Victoria Sch., Seychelles, 23rd Aug., 1903.

McKEAN, Lieut.-Col. ALEXANDER CHALMERS, C.M.G. (1891).—B. 1852; cornet, Inniskilling Dragoons, Oct., 1871; A.D.C., Bengal, 1880; served in Transvaal war, 1881; staff off., Zululand war (Eshowe column), 1883; D.A.A. and Q.M.G., S. Africa, 1884; ag. D.A.A.G., Natal, 1886; survr. to Zululand and New Republic boundary comm., 1886; asst. comsnr., Zululand, 1887; comsnr. of Basuto levies in Zulu disturbances, 1888; was honourably mentioned and made brevet lieut.-col. for services; asst. mil. sec. to gov., Malta, 1889.

MACKENZIE, DONALD.—Ch. inspr. of pol., Penang, Dec., 1887; ag. survr. pol., Sungei Ujong, Apr., 1890.

MACKENZIE RIVER, Bishop of, THE RIGHT REV. WM. D. RERVES.—C.M., Coll., Isl., 1865; consec. 1891; hon. D.D., St. John's Coll., Manitoba, 1891; missionary, (C.M.S.) at Fort Simpson, Mackenzie River, &c.; chapl. to Bishop of Athabasca, 1874-84; archd. Chipewyan, 1883-98.

McKINSTRY, W. L.—Barrister-at-law, Lincoln's Inn; ed. Harr. Coll., Barbados; passed civ. ser. test exam. 1882; supernum. coll. sec.'s office, 1883; ag. clk. audit office, exec. comte.'s office, col. sec.'s office, and as sec. to poor law bd., 1886 and 1888; clk. in petty debt ct., Jan., 1889; elk. to inspr.-gen. of pol., June, 1889; ag. inspr. of pol. and asst. of fire brig., 1889-91; int. rev. offr., 1892; transf. to customs, 1896; ag. gov., Glendairy prison, May to Nov., 1904.

McLEAN, THE HON. ALLAN.—M.L.A., Victoria; pres. of bd. of land and wks. and comsnr. of crown lands and survey, Nov., 1890, to Feb., 1892; min. of agric., Nov., 1890, to Apil., 1891; chief sec., Apil., 1891, to Feb., 1892; ch. sec., pres., bd. of land and wks., comsnr. of lands and survey, Feb., 1892, to Jan., 1893; premier and ch. sec., Dec., 1899, to Nov., 1900; min. for trade and customs, commonwealth parl., Oct., 1904.

McLELLAN, DAVID.—Men. of house of assem. and exec. coun., New Brunswick; prov. sec. and rec.-gen.; pres. of exec. coun., 1890.

MACLEOD, NEIL.—Called to the bar, P.E.I., 1872; mem. of house of assem. since 1879; prov. sec. and treas., 1879 to 1882; atty.-gen. and premier, 1889.

MACLEOD, NORMAN MAGNUS, C.M.G. (1890).—B. 1839; late capt. 74th Highlanders; was comdt. of Swazi contingent against Sikukuni, 1879.

MACLURE, WILLIAM GRANT.—Admtd. Bahamas Bar, 1889; asst. clk., House of Assem., 1890; J.P. for col. and prov. res. just., Gov.'s Harbour, 1894; acted as stip. and circuit mag. and coroner, Is. of New Providence; regist., sup. ct., Bahamas, 1898.

MCMILLAN, SIR DANIEL HUNTER, K.C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1846; Ed. Canada; served with Canadian Volunteers on Niagara frontier, 1864; during Fenian raid, 1866; Red River expdn., 1870; N.W. rebellion (medal), 1885; mem. for Winnipeg in Manitoba legislature, 1886; mem. of Manitoba govt., 1889; lt.-gov. of Manitoba, 6th Sept., 1900.

MCMILLAN, ROBERT FURSE.—Queen's scholar, Westminster school; scholar, Trin. Hall, Camb.; senior in law tripes, 1879; holder of law studentship at Trin. Hall; Inns of Court studentship and Inner Temple common law scholarship; called to the bar, 1881; joined western circuit and Devon and Exeter sessions; puisne judge, W. Australia, 1903.

McNAIR, J. F. A., C.M.G. (1879).—B. 1828; major, Roy. (late Madras) Artill. (retd.); ed. at King's Coll., Lond.; and student at the Schl. of Mines; entered the Madras Artill. in 1845; served in India, the S. Sttlmtns., and Labuan; priv. sec. to the gov. S.S., 1857; and subsequently exec. engrn. and supt. of convicts, Singapore; ch. engrn., S.S., on their transfer to the crown in 1867; accompanied the gov. to Siam, Aug., 1867; survr. gen. S.S., 1872; ch. comsnr. of Perak throughout the disturbances in that country in 1875-6, and engaged in the affair at Kotah Lama, on the Perak river; special comsnr. to Selangore to inquire into piracy, and to Perak in connection with the Pangkor treaty, 1874; again to Siam, in Aug. of that year, on special mission; again, in 1875, with Sir A. Clarke, in connection with unsettled state of affairs there; special mission to the State of Sungei Ujong, 1878; sec. to Sir W. Robinson's mission to Siam in Nov., 1878, to present the G.C.M.G. to the king; author of "Perak and the Malays," &c.; ag. lieut.-gov. and res. councillor of Penang from Feb., 1881, to Aug., 1884, when he ret.

MACNAGHTEN, T. C.—Ed. Charterhouse and Oxford; scholar of Hertford Coll., 1892; 1st class classical mods., 1894; B.A., 1896; apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd class clk., Local Govt. Bd., Feb., 1896; 2nd class clk., C.O., Sept., 1896; priv. sec. to Earl of Selborne, Dec., 1899, to Earl of Onslow, Nov., 1900, to Duke of Marlborough, July, 1903; 1st cl. clk., 24th Mch., 1904.

MCNEIL, MAJ.-GEN. SIR JOHN CARSTAIRS, G.C.B. (1882), K.C.M.G. (1880), C.M.G. (1870), V.C.—B. 1831; served during campaign of 1857-58 in India as A.D.C. to Sir E. Lugard during the siege and capture of Lucknow; in 1861-5 A.D.C. to Sir D. Cameron in N. Zealand; commanded Tipperary flying column during Fenian disturbances, 1866-67; served on the staff of Red River expdn. under Sir G. Wolseley in 1870, and in the Ashanti war, 1873-74; A.D.C. to H.R.H. the Duke of Cambridge, Jan., 1874, and an equerry to Her Majesty in Aug. following; served in the Egyptian expdn., 1882, personally attached to the Duke of Connaught; served in the Soudan expdn., 1885; commanded troops at the action of Tobrek, for which clasp was granted.

MOWAN, ISLAY.—3rd clk., col. sec.'s off., Fiji, Sept., 1892; stip. mag., asst. to native comsnr., and tax inspr., Lau, May, 1896; stip. mag. and tax inspr., Navua, and comsnr. for Namasi, Feb., 1900; stip. mag., Lomaiviti and Tailevu; comsnr. and tax inspr., Lomaiviti; offr. in charge, Levuka gaol, Jan., 1904.

MACPHERSON, A.—Served during S. A. war in Lord Dunraven's sharpshooters; civilian warrant offr. and paymaster, Imperial remount farm, 1st to 14th Dec., 1902; ch. clk. and sen. examr. of accts., audit dept., O.R.C., 15th Dec., 1902.
MACPHERSON, LT.-COL. JOHN.—Acctnt. and ch. clk. store branch dept. of militia and defence, Canada, Sept., 1872; dir. of stores and keeper of militia properties, Nov., 1880.

McTURK, MICHAEL, C.M.G. (1897).—B. 1843; revenue offr. and asst. survr., Essequibo, 1872; comsnr. of taxation, Essequibo dist., 1873; special mag. and supt. crown lands and forests, Essequibo, 1878; govt. gold mining offr., Br. Guiana, 1887.

MACWILLIAM, DONALD KIRTON.—2nd clk., treasry., St. Kitts, 1894; rev. offr. and quarantine offr., Apr., 1894.

MADDEN, SIR JOHN, K.C., K.C.M.G. (1899), KT. BACH. (1893).—B. 1844; ch. justice of Victoria, 1893; administered the govt., 1893, 1895, 1897, and 1898, and again, as lieut.-gov., Jan., 1900-1.

MADDEN, W.—Pres. bd. of land and wks., and comsnr., crown lands and survey, Victoria, Aug., 1881, to Mar., 1883.

MADLEY, LEWIS GEORGE.—Col. S. Australian Militia Infantry; principal of training coll., educn. dept., S.A., 1876; also D.A.A.G. of S.A. mil. forces, 1895; comsnr. of pol., 1896.

MAGRATH, THOS. HENRY.—Jun. clk., P.O., Tasmania, 1853; ch. clk., 1869; comptroller of money orders, 1879, and of savings bank, 1882; sec. to P.O., 1888.

MAGRO, PROF. E., M.D.—Grad. Malta Univ., 1877; examr. in arts and sciences, 1882; examr. in med. and surgery, 1884; prof. of math. and physics, Oct., 1885; examr. in land surveying and archt., Oct., 1885; ag. princ. and sec. to the univ., 1887; dir. of educn. and sec. to the senate, 1888-97; ag. inspr. in charge of elemen. schls., Jan., 1898; sec. to Oxford local exams. in Malta, 1898; mem. ex. coun. and of coun. of govt., 1902.

MAHAFFY, ARTHUR W.—Ed. at Marlborough, and Magdalen Coll., Oxford, demy, 1889; B.A., Dublin Univ. (Trin. Coll.); 2nd lieut., 1st Batt. Royal Munster Fusiliers, 1892-1896; gov. agt. Gilbert Is. Prot., Oct., 1896; asst. to res. comsnr., Solomon Is., 1897; res. mag., W. division, Solomon Is., and dep. comsnr. for W. Pacific, 1899; col. sec. and recvr.-gen., Fiji, Oct., 1904.

MAHONY, LIEUT.-COL. JOHN, C.M.G. (1879).—B. 1824; paymr., army pay dept., in the Zulu war; ret. with the hon. rank of lieut.-col., Mar., 1884.

MAITLAND, ANDREW GILBERT.—Reed. his educn. as a geologist and civil engr. at Yorkshire Coll. of Science, Leeds; graduated, 1885; asst. govt. geologist, Queensland, 1888; his official duties taking him as far afield as Br. N. Guinea; govt. geol. of W. Australia, 1896; has written several works on the geology, features, and mineral resources of Queensland and W. Australia.

MAJOR, CHARLES.—Called to the Bar (Mid. Temp.), June, 1887; mem. of Leeward Is. bar, Sept., 1887; chancellor of the diocese of Antigua, Oct., 1889; nominated mem. of legis. coun., Antigua, 1895 to 1899; nominated mem. of gen. legis. coun., Leewards, Nov., 1896, and pres. of same, Dec., 1896, to 1899; mem. fed. ex. couns., Leewards, Mar., 1897, to June, 1901; vice-pres. legis. coun., Antigua, May, 1897; ag. sol.-gen. and atty.-gen., Leewards, 1897, 1898, 1899; capt. commanding Antigua volunteer defence force on its establishment, 1897; J.P., 1897; ag. 2nd puisne judge, Leewards, June, 1899; atty.-gen. of Grenada, 1901; ch. just. of Fiji, and chief judicial comsnr. of Western Pacific, 1902; admnstd. govt., Mar.-Oct., 1904.

MAJOR, F. W.—5th clk., treasry., Trinidad, Oct., 1885; 2nd clk. to supt. of prisons, Jan., 1886; 9th clk., audit office, Aug., 1887; 8th clk., 1888; priv. sec. to Sir W. Robinson, 1888; super. of customs, G. Coast, Feb., 1891; ass. comptroller of customs, 1891; asst. treas., Aug., 1891; ag. comptroller of customs, various dates from 1891 to 1895; comptroller of customs, Nov., 1895; rec.-gen., Bermuda, 1899.

MALCOLM, DOUGAL ORME.—Ed. at Eton and New Coll., Oxford; 1st cl. mods., 1897; 1st cl. lit. hum., 1899; B.A., 1899; Fellow of All Soul., 1899; M.A., 1902; apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd cl. clk., C.O. Oct., 1900.

MALCOLM, HARCOURT GASTON.—Pri. sec. to Sir Henry Jackson when admnstr. of Bahamas, 1892, 1893, 1895; ditto to Sir W. F. Hayne-Smith, gov. of Bahamas, 1895; called to the bar, Lincoln's Inn, June, 1899; ditto, Bahamas, July, 1899; mem. of house of ass., Bahamas, 1900; deputy-speaker, 1901; re-elected, 1904.

MALCOLM, SIR ORMOND DRUMMIE, KT. BACH. (1898).—B. 1839; called to the bar of the Bahamas, July, 1861; ag. pol. mag. in 1864 and 1866; elected mem. of house of assem. in 1865; speake., 1868; ag. judge, court of common pleas, 1875; Q.C. in 1876; ag. atty-gen., Mar., 1882; ag. admnstr., June, 1896; ch. just. of Bahama Is., 1897.

MALING, CAPT. IRWIN CHAR., C.M.G. (1892).—B. 1841; ed. at Wimbledon schl. and Roy. Mil. Acad.; late 23rd Roy. Welsh Fus.; dep. mag. and collr., Nuddes dist., Bengal, 1857; served throughout the Indian mutiny, 1857-59; present in many engagements (medal); ensign, 1861, 89th Princess Victoria's Regt.; priv. sec. and A.D.C. to the gov., W. Coast of Africa, 1868; lieut. 36th Roy. Sussex Regt., 1870; priv. sec. to the Marquis of Normanby, gov. of Queensland, 1871, and New Zealand, 1874; col. sec. and regir. gen. of Grenada, 1879; administ. the govt. in 1880, 1882, 184-47; ag. col. sec., Leeward Is., 1889; and represve. at quarantine confce. at Demera, 1888; ag. admnstr., 1889; adminstr. of St. Vincent, 1889; ret. 1893.

MALONEY, HENRY.—Curator, Botanic Station, Montserrat; sanitary offr., Jan., 1897.

MALSCH, CHARLES CHRISTIAN, A.M.I.C.E.—Draughtsman, works dept., admiralty, 1866; ast engnr., German admiralty wks., Kiel, 1873; survr. state engnr. dept., California; surveying Sacramento and Fraser Rivers, etc., California and Br. Columbia, 1875; exploring Formosa for Chinese govt., 1881 to 1883; ast. engnr., P.W. dept., Hong Kong, 1884; supt. of crown land, 1892; ag. assessor of rates, 1894; J.P., 1894.

MANN, MAJ.-GEN. J. R., R.E., C.M.G. (1881).—B. 1823; entered R.E., 1840; survr.-gen. of Mauritius, 1856 to 1861; dir. of roads and survr.-gen. of Jamaica, 1867; resig. 1873, and re-apptd. in Feb., 1874; official, M.L.C., 1874; ret., 1886.

MANNING, ALBERT EDWARD.—Copyist in registrar's office, Br. Guiana; ast. sworn clk., 1887; sworn clk. and notary public, 1898; comsnr. to administer oaths and affidavits, 1900.

MANSEL, GEORGE, C.M.G. (1891).—Served in Weenen Yeomanry through the Langalibalele rebellion in 1873; served as sub.-inspr. and inspr. in Natal mounted pol. through Zulu war, 1879 (medal with clasp), and Boer war, 1880 and 1881; raised and commanded the Reserve Territory Carbineers from 1883 to 1887, when the force was changed into the Zululand pol.; served in this force through all disturbances in Zululand from 1883 to 1888; twice mentioned in despatches as having shown conspicuous coolness and gallantry.
MANSERGH, CORNEWALL LEWIS WARWICKSHIRE.—Ck., crown lands office, Capetown, May, 1880; 2nd cl. ck. and priv. sec. to comnr. of crown lands and pub. wks., May, 1884; 1st cl. ck., Apr., 1892; ch. ck. to the ast. comnr. of rly. and pub. wks., Oct., 1892; sec. pub. wks., July, 1898.

MANSON, SIR PATRICK, K.C.M.G. (1903); C.M.G. (1900); M.D., F.R.C.P., LL.D.—B. 1844; late dean and lect. on med. coll. of med. for Chinese, Hong Kong; phys. Seamen's Hospital Soc. at Albert Docks branch; lect. on trop. diseases, St. George's and Charing Cross Hosps.; apptd. med. adviser to C.O., 1897.

MARKS, OLIVER.—Supt. govt. plants, Perak, Mar., 1891; 2nd cls. mag., Apl., 1894; ag. ast. mag., Kinta, July, 1894; ast. mag., Kinta, July, 1896; ag. ast. sec. to govt., Perak, Sep., 1896; ast. sec. to govt., Perak, May, 1897; passed Malay, Mar., 1898; 1st cls. mag., June, 1898; ast. sec. to res. gen., Fed. Malay States, Nov., 1898; ag. sec. to res. gen., F. M. S., Mar., 1899; sec. to high comnr., F. M. S., Aug., 1903.

MARLBOROUGH, 9TH Duke OF (created, 1702), CHARLES RICHARD JOHN SPENCER-CHURCHILL, P.C., K.G.—B. 1871; Chancellor of Primrose League, 1897 and 1898; served with yeomanry cavalry, S. Africa, 1900, and A.D.C. to Lieut.-Gen. Sir Ian Hamilton, K.C.B.; pay-master-general, 1899; under-sec. of state for the colonies, July, 1903.

MARRIOTT, H., B.A., 1st cls. math. tripso, Cantab.—Cadet S. Sttlmts., Nov., 1896; ag. 3rd mag., Singapore, May, 1897; passed fin. exam. in Malay, May, 1898; dist. offr., Malacca, Feb., 1899; ag. 2nd mag., Sing., Feb., 1902; ast. P.M.G., Penang, Sept., 1903; ag. 2nd mag., Penang, July, 1904.

MARSH, EDWARD HOWARD.—Ed. at Westminster and Cambridge; scholar, Trin. Coll., 1891; 1st cl. classical tripso, 1893; sen. chancellor's medal for classics, 1895; 1st cl. with distinction classical tripso, Part II., and B.A., 1896; M.A., 1897; apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd cl. ck., C.O., Sept., 29, 1896; ast. priv. sec. to Mr. Chamberlain, July, 1900; to Mr. Lyttleton, Oct., 1903.

MARSH, HERBERT.—Cadet, S. Sttlmts., 27th Nov., 1903.

MARSH, T. R., C.M.G. (1901), on retirement from post as head of the contract branch, crown agents' office; B. 1847.

MARSH, SIR WILLIAM HENRY, K.C.M.G. (1887), C.M.G. (1881).—B. 1827; Clk. to procureur-gen. Mauritius, Feb., 1848; crown solr., Apl., 1854; ch. ck., col. sec.'s office, Oct., 1859; special immigr. comnr. to India, May, 1865; jun. ast. col. sec., Apl., 1866; sen. ast. col. sec., 1867; sole ast., 1870; ag. col. sec., 1875-6; audr.-gen., Apl., 1876; col. sec. and audr.-gen., Hong Kong, 1879; ag. audr. and acctnt.-gen., Cyprus, 1881; adminstr. govt. Hong Kong on six occasions; ret., 1887.

MARSHALL, ARTHUR LACY.—Clerical ast., immigr. dept., Br. Guiana, Dec., 1875; supernumerary clk., 1876; clerical ast. to col. sec., Tobago, 1879; 2nd rev. offr., May, 1882; 1st rev. offr., Apl., 1885; ch. ck., treas., July, 1885.

MARSHALL, COLONEL ROBERT SETON.—Lieut. 3rd brig. Scottish div. R.A., 1882; (lieut. reserve of offrs., 1885); capt., 1885; instructor of artillery, 1887; (capt., rea. of offrs. 1896); major Edin. artill. militia, 1896; (hon. major in the army, 1900); hon. lt.-col., 1903; lt.-col., 1903; retired with hon. rank of col., 1903; served with the 1st brig. W. div. R.A., 1885; staff offr. local forces, Trinidad, Sept., 1888, to Dec., 1891; sec. local defence comtee., 1888; command of Trinidad artill. volrs. for purpose of organising the corps, 1888; A.D.C. to offr. admnstr. govt. of Trin. and Tobago, May to Dec., 1889; ag. commdt. Trinidad local forces, 6th-19th Nov., 1890; adjt. and musketry instr., Br. Guiana pol., Dec., 1891; ag. adjt. Br. G. militia, May to Oct., 1894; and Aug. to Sept., 1897; ag. inspr. of Br. G. pol. during period of special employment at Ururan frontier station, Oct., 1895, to Mar., 1896; adjt. of Br. G. militia and police, Dec., 1897; ag. commdt. Br. G. militia, 9th May to 22nd Aug., 1900; sent to frontier to hand over Amacura and Barima Sands to Venezuela, Oct., 1900; sent to Trinidad for special duty with police, after the riot, 2nd to 27th May, 1903.

MARTIN, H. A.—Ag. ck. to auditor, Grenada, Aug., 1884, to June, 1885; ck. to promarshal, June to July, 1885; ag. ch. to audr., May to Nov., 1887; ast. ck., treasy., Jan., 1889; ag. wks. acctnt., Jan. to Oct., 1-90; ch. ck., regiar., Nov., 1891; treasy. acctnt., St. Lucia and Grenada, Apr., 1894; supt. prisons, Feb. to May, 1897; 2nd financial ast., P.W.D., Ceylon, June, 1897.

MARTIN, JAMES H.—Apptd., after exam., messenger Admity., Aug., 1875; transf. C.O., Sept., 1877; Queen's meas., June, 1897.

MARTIN, JOSEPH.—Mem. of legis. assem., and exec. coun., Manitoba; atty.-gen. and comnr. of rlys. and lands.

MARTIN, LOUIS.—Volr. in survr.-gen.'s dept. at Mauritius, Dec., 1859; ck. in audit office, Jan., 1860; jun. examnr., Mar., 1862; sen. examnr., Sept., 1869; ch. ck., immigr. dept., Mar., 1870; col. postmr. and supt. of telegraphs, May, 1890.

MARTIN, COL. SIR RICHARD EDWARD ROWLEY, K.C.M.G. (1895), C.M.G. (1888), Inniskilling Dragoons.—B. 1847; commanded mounted infantry at Cetywayo's installation, Zululand, 1883; commdt. of gen. depot, Bechuanaland field force, 1884; major Bechuanaland border pol., 1885 to 1887; was Br. comnr.-pres., Portuguese-Swazi bdry., comnr., and Br. comnr. on special mission to Tongaland, 1888; proceeded on visit of inquiry to Swaziland, 1889; sec. to Br. comnr. to Swaziland, 1889; Br. mem. of temporary joint coman. of adminstr., 1889-95; commdt. of pol. and dep. coms., Rhodesia, Mar., 1896.

MARTIN, S. B.—Ed. Wesleyan Mission Schl., C. Coast; 6th class offr., customs, G. Coast, Sept., 1890; ck. to dir. of telegraphs and store-keeper, Aug., 1891; ck. and acctnt., July, 1893.

MARTINS, FRED. G.—Ed. C.M.S. Coll. Inst., Lagos; jun. bailiff, sup. ct., June, 1884; ck. to Queen's advoc., Aug., 1886; storekeeper, P.W. dept., Jan., 1891; audit ck., Jan., 1895.

MARTINS, G. N.—Ed. C.M.S. Grammar Schl., Lagos; messenger, audit, and P.O., 1889; customs, outdoor offr., 1890 to 1893 (during which time attached to revenue office); ag. ck., P.O., 1893; 4th ck. of customs, 1893; 3rd ck. and statistician, Mar., 1894; transf. to the revenue dept., 1900; deputy for cashier and ch. ck. on various occasions; 2nd cls. ck., customs, 1901.

MARWOOD, HORACE RICHARD, A.M.I.C.E.—Junr. ast. engrnr., Taff Vale rlyws., 1877; supernumerary 2nd cl. ast. engrnr. Cape Govt. rlyws. (Eastern system), 1882; 1st cl. ast. W. system, 1883, also in charge of district, 1884; ast. engrnr. rlyws. service of H.H. the Sultan of Selangor, S.S. 1885; chef-de-division, Pyraeus Larissa rlyws.,
Greece, 1890; engrnr. of wks. and maintenance Trinidad govt. rlyss., 1894.

MASKELL, THOS. AUGUSTUS CORNELIUS.—Cler. astt. to inspr. of schls., B. Guiana, June, 1873; clk., Apl., 1891; 3rd cls. clk., Apl., 1893; sec. to educn. comsnr., 1902.

MASON, ARTHUR WIER, B.A.—Puise judge, sup. ct., Natal, 1896; ag. ch. just., 1900-01; comsnr. of spec. treason ct., 1900-01; pres. of ditto, 1901-02; puise judge, sup. ct., Transvaal, 1902.

MASON, CLAYTON T., M.I.C.E., J.P.—Ed. King Edward's Schll., Birmingham; from 1874 to 1877 was engaged in the rly. branch of the dept. of pub. wks., N. S. Wales; res. engrnr. of the Geraldton and Northampton rly., W. Australia, 1877; suptd. the construction of Point Moore Lighthouse and other pub. wks. in the Victoria dist.; afterwards res. engrnr. for four years of the E. rly. in the same col.; ag. comsnr. of rlys. on two occasions during 1882 and 1883; was provisionally apptd. in 1884 dir. of pub. wks. and comsnr. of rlys.; mem. of the exec. and legis. couns., gen. man. and maintenance engrnr., June, 1885; comsnr. of rlys. and mem. of exec. coun., Jan., 1890; after the introduction of responsible govt. was apptd. collr. of customs, June, 1891.

MASON, GERALD BOVELL.—Ed. Harrison Coll., Barbados; matric., London Univ., 1890; joined London hosp., 1890; passed prelim. scientific, 1892; M.R.C.S.(Eng.), L.R.C.P.(Lond.), 1896; jun. ast. med. offr., St. Marylebone infirmary, 1896; clin. astt., aural and ophthalmic depts., Lond. hosp., 1897; house physician, Brompton hosp., 1898; priv. sec. to Sir C. Quilter, Bart., M.P., on voyage to W. Indies, 1891; ag. med. offr., Three Counties asylum, 1891; civ. surg. in charge, Station hosp., Woking, 1892; apptd. med. offr., No. 4 dist., Antigua, 1903; ag. comsnr., Virgin Is., 1904; surg.-lieut., Antigua dist. force, 1904.

MASSON, HON. LOUIS FRANCOIS RODERIQUE.—Called to the bar of Lower Canada, 1859; brigade-major, 8th military dist. of Lower Canada, from 1863 to 1868, and holds the rank of lieut.-col. in the militia; entered Canadian parlmt., 1867; sworn of the privy coun. of Canada and apptd. min. of militia and defence, 19th Oct., 1878; ret., 1880; called to the senate, 1882, and to the legis. coun. of the province, 1890; Quebec, 1884; gov. of Quebec, 1884-7; senator, 1890.

MATHEWS, HENRY ADOLPHUS.—Passed through govt. training instr., B. Guiana; 1st cls. certificated schlinstr.; head-master, grant-in-aid schl., B. Guiana, 9½ yrs.; educntl. dist. offr., 15th Nov., 1893; acted as 2nd astt. inspr. of schools on various occasions, 1895-1903.
